questions.stem: A report builder creates `Supplier<String> stamp = clock.instant()::toString;` at 09:00. Each call to `clock.instant()` returns the time of that call. The builder calls `stamp.get()` at 09:05 and again at 09:10. What do the two calls return?

options.text: 09:00 both times, since `clock.instant()` ran once, when `stamp` was created
options.says: a bound reference evaluates the expression before :: when the reference is created and keeps the result

options.text: 09:05 both times, since `clock.instant()` ran once, when `stamp.get()` was first called
options.says: the receiver is not evaluated lazily on the first call; it is evaluated when the reference is created

options.text: 09:05, then 09:10, since `clock.instant()` runs again on each call, as a lambda body would
options.says: only a lambda re-runs its receiver expression on every call; a bound reference evaluated it once

options.text: Nothing, since the code before `::` must be a variable or a type name, so this does not compile
options.says: any expression can stand before :: in a bound reference; counter.next()::toString compiled and ran

origin.section: A Bound Receiver Is Evaluated Once, When the Reference Is Created

questions.stem: At startup a service runs `Function<String, String> toLocal = registry.lookup("eu")::translate;` and keeps `toLocal` in a map; it is called only when a request from that region arrives. In this deployment `lookup("eu")` returns `null`. What happens?

options.text: Startup fails on that line with a `NullPointerException` that has no message, since the receiver is checked when `toLocal` is created
options.says: javac emits Objects.requireNonNull on the receiver before creating the object, so the NPE is thrown at creation and carries no message

options.text: Startup fails on that line with a `NullPointerException` whose message names `lookup("eu")`, since the receiver is checked when `toLocal` is created
options.says: the check is Objects.requireNonNull, which throws without a message; only an NPE from a dereference gets the helpful message

options.text: Startup succeeds, and the first request from that region gets a `NullPointerException` whose message names `lookup("eu")`, since the receiver is read when `toLocal` is called
options.says: that is how the lambda () -> registry.lookup("eu").translate(s) behaves; the reference reads and checks its receiver at creation

options.text: Startup succeeds, and the first request from that region gets a `NullPointerException` that has no message, since the receiver is read when `toLocal` is called
options.says: the receiver is read and checked when the reference is created, so startup fails; nothing waits for the first request

origin.section: A Null Receiver Fails Where the Reference Is Created

questions.stem: A class has one method, whose body is `orders.stream().map(Order::total).map(t -> t * 2).toList(); orders.forEach(audit::record);`. `Order` is a record nested in the same class, `audit` is a parameter, and `record(Order)` is an ordinary instance method. How many `lambda$` methods does `javap -p` list for the class (javac 21)?

options.text: One, since only the lambda needs a method of the class to hold its code
options.says: Order::total and audit::record are handed to LambdaMetafactory as direct method handles; only the lambda body becomes lambda$…

options.text: Two, since the lambda and the bound reference each need a method of the class
options.says: a bound receiver is passed as an argument of the invokedynamic, like a captured value; it needs no adapter method

options.text: Three, since every lambda and every method reference needs a method of the class
options.says: unbound and bound references point straight at their target; only varargs, array constructors and super:: got an adapter

options.text: None, since a lambda with one expression also gets a direct handle, like a reference
options.says: the one-expression lambda s -> s.length() got its own lambda$ method; only a reference already names a method

origin.section: javac Points Most Method References Straight at the Method, With No lambda$ Method in Between

questions.stem: In production, `names.stream().map(String::trim).map(String::toUpperCase).toList()` meets a `null` element. What does the logged `NullPointerException` show (Java 21, default JVM flags)?

options.text: No message, and a frame of the stream's `map` stage on top, since the frame that made the failing call is not shown
options.says: the call happens in the generated hidden class, whose frame the JVM leaves out, and without it the JVM gives the NPE no message

options.text: No message, and a frame of `String.trim` on top, since the exception starts in the JDK method handed the null
options.says: trim is never entered: the call on a null receiver fails in the caller, which is the hidden frame

options.text: A message naming `String.trim()`, and a frame of `String.trim` on top, since the exception starts in the JDK method handed the null
options.says: trim is never entered, and the NPE comes from a hidden frame, so it has neither that frame nor a message

options.text: A message naming `String.trim()`, and a frame of the stream's `map` stage on top, since the message is built from the call that failed
options.says: the helpful message is computed from the method that threw, which is hidden here, so the NPE has no message

origin.section: A Stack Trace Through a Method Reference Has No Frame of Its Own
